```text
func (m *Model) View() tea.View {
	var content string
	if m.quitting {
		return tea.NewView("")
	}
	if m.width < 30 || m.height < 8 {
		content = "lazypkg · " + viewNames[m.view] + "\nResize for package actions.\nq quit · Esc back"
	} else if m.modal != noModal {
		content = m.modalView()
	} else {
		content = m.dashboardView()
	}
	content = fitScreen(content, m.width, m.height)
	if _, ok := os.LookupEnv("NO_COLOR"); ok {
		content = ansi.Strip(content)
	}
	v := tea.NewView(content)
	v.AltScreen = true
	v.WindowTitle = "lazypkg"
	if focused {
		style = style.BorderForeground(lipgloss.Color("#7AC7E3"))
	} else {
		style = style.BorderForeground(lipgloss.Color("#586273"))
	}
	return style.Render(strings.Join(lines, "\n"))
}

func clean(s string) string {
	s = ansi.Strip(s)
	s = strings.Map(func(r rune) rune {
		if r == '\n' || r == '\t' {
			return r
		}
		if unicode.IsControl(r) {
			return -1
		}
		return r
	}, s)
	return strings.ReplaceAll(s, "\t", "  ")
}

func line(s string, width int) string {
	width = max(1, width)
	s = ansi.Truncate(s, width, "…")
	return s + strings.Repeat(" ", max(0, width-ansi.StringWidth(s)))
}

func wrapLines(s string, width int) []string {
	return strings.Split(ansi.Hardwrap(clean(s), max(1, width), true), "\n")
}

func fitScreen(s string, width, height int) string {
	lines := strings.Split(s, "\n")

		lines = lines[:height]
```

```text
func (v semver) String() string { return fmt.Sprintf("%d.%d.%d", v.major, v.minor, v.patch) }
func (v semver) compare(w semver) int {
	for i, x := range []int{v.major, v.minor, v.patch} {
		y := []int{w.major, w.minor, w.patch}[i]
		if x < y {
			return -1
		}
		if x > y {
			return 1
		}
	}
	return 0
}
func version(text string) (semver, bool) {
	text = strings.TrimSpace(text)
	for _, word := range strings.Fields(text) {
		word = strings.TrimPrefix(strings.TrimPrefix(word, "go"), "v")
		if strings.ContainsAny(word, "-+") {
			continue
		}
		parts := strings.Split(word, ".")
		if len(parts) != 3 {
			continue
		}
		var values [3]int
		ok := true
		for i, p := range parts {
			n, err := strconv.Atoi(p)
			if err != nil || n < 0 {
				ok = false
				break
			}
			values[i] = n
		}
		if ok {
			return semver{values[0], values[1], values[2]}, true
		}
	}
	return semver{}, false
}
func minimum(v semver, requirement string) bool {
	r := strings.TrimSpace(requirement)
	if r == "" {
		return true
	}
	r = strings.TrimPrefix(r, ">=")
	if w, ok := version(r); ok {
		return v.compare(w) >= 0
	}
	ok, known := satisfies(v, requirement)
	return known && ok
}
```

```bash
package domain

import (
	"regexp"
	"strconv"
	"strings"
)

// UpdateKind describes how far an available version is from the installed one.
// It is derived from version text for display only and never gates an upgrade.
type UpdateKind string

const (
	UpdateMajor    UpdateKind = "major"
	UpdateMinor    UpdateKind = "minor"
	UpdatePatch    UpdateKind = "patch"
	UpdateRevision UpdateKind = "revision" // same upstream version, rebuilt (brew _N, cask build)
	UpdateUnknown  UpdateKind = ""
)

var dateVersion = regexp.MustCompile(`^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}`)

type parsedVersion struct {
	numbers  []int
	pre      string
	revision string
	calendar bool
}

func parseVersion(text string) (parsedVersion, bool) {
	text = strings.TrimPrefix(strings.TrimSpace(text), "v")
	if text == "" {
		return parsedVersion{}, false
	}
	if dateVersion.MatchString(text) {
		return parsedVersion{calendar: true}, true
	}
	var v parsedVersion
	// Homebrew casks append a build after a comma; formulae append a revision after an underscore.
	if core, build, ok := strings.Cut(text, ","); ok {
		text, v.revision = core, build
	}
	if i := strings.LastIndex(text, "_"); i > 0 {
		v.revision = text[i+1:] + v.revision
		text = text[:i]
	}
	if i := strings.IndexAny(text, "-+"); i > 0 {
		text, v.pre = text[:i], text[i:]
	}
	for _, part := range strings.Split(text, ".") {
		n, err := strconv.Atoi(part)
		if err != nil || n < 0 {
			return parsedVersion{}, false
		}
		v.numbers = append(v.numbers, n)
	}
	v.calendar = v.numbers[0] >= 1000
	return v, true
}

// ClassifyUpdate reports the semantic distance from installed to latest.
// Calendar, unparseable or non-increasing versions are UpdateUnknown. For 0.x
// versions a minor change is treated as major and a patch change as minor,
// following semantic versioning's initial-development rule.
func ClassifyUpdate(installed, latest string) UpdateKind {
	a, okA := parseVersion(installed)
	b, okB := parseVersion(latest)
	if !okA || !okB || a.calendar || b.calendar {
		return UpdateUnknown
	}
	for i := range max(len(a.numbers), len(b.numbers)) {
		x, y := segment(a.numbers, i), segment(b.numbers, i)
		if x == y {
			continue
		}
		if y < x {
			return UpdateUnknown
		}
		if a.numbers[0] == 0 && i > 0 {
			i--
		}
		switch i {
		case 0:
			return UpdateMajor
		case 1:
			return UpdateMinor
		default:
			return UpdatePatch
		}
	}
	if a.pre != b.pre {
		return UpdatePatch
	}
	if a.revision != b.revision {
		return UpdateRevision
	}
	return UpdateUnknown
}

func segment(numbers []int, i int) int {
	if i < len(numbers) {
		return numbers[i]
	}
	return 0
}

// UpdateKind classifies the package's installed version against its latest.
func (p Package) UpdateKind() UpdateKind { return ClassifyUpdate(p.Version, p.Latest) }
EOF
```

```text
func (m *Model) packagePane(width, height int) string {
	rows := m.rows(m.view)
	s := &m.states[m.view]
	var lines []string
	if len(rows) == 0 {
		lines = wrapLines(m.emptyText(), max(1, width-4))
	} else {
		heading := "Item"
		if m.view == diagnosticsView {
			heading = "Finding / executable"
		} else if m.view == managersView {
			heading = "Provider"
		}
		lines = append(lines, muted.Render(fmt.Sprintf("%s · %d", heading, len(rows))))
		count := max(1, height-5)
		start := clamp(s.offset, 0, max(0, len(rows)-count))
		for i := start; i < min(start+count, len(rows)); i++ {
			r := rows[i]
			marker := "  "
			if r.key == s.selected {
				marker = "> "
			}
			if packageView(m.view) && r.pkg != nil {
				check := "  "
				if _, marked := s.marks[r.key]; marked {
					check = "✓ "
				} else if ok, _ := m.upgradeEligibility(m.view, *r.pkg); !ok {
					check = "! "
				}
				marker += check
			}
			secondary := r.secondary
			if r.manager != "" && m.view != managersView {
				secondary = providerLabel(r.manager) + " · " + secondary
			}
			available := max(1, width-4)
			var value string
			if available >= 38 {
				right := min(25, available/2)
				value = marker + line(clean(r.label), available-right-1-ansi.StringWidth(marker)) + " " + line(clean(secondary), right)
			} else {
				value = marker + clean(r.label)
			}
			value = line(value, width-2)
			if r.key == s.selected && !m.managerFocus {
				value = selectedStyle.Render(value)
			}
			lines = append(lines, value)
		}
		if len(rows) > count {
			lines = append(lines, muted.Render(fmt.Sprintf("%d–%d of %d", start+1, min(start+count, len(rows)), len(rows))))
		}
	}
	return pane(viewNames[m.view], lines, width, height, !m.managerFocus)
}

func (m *Model) emptyText() string {
	s := &m.states[m.view]
	if m.view == managersView {
		if m.managersLoading {
			return "Detecting package managers…\n\nYou can switch views while this runs."
		}
		if m.managersErr != nil {
			return "Manager discovery could not finish.\n\nPress e for the error or s to set up the backend."
		}
		if !m.showAllManagers && len(m.managers) > 0 {
			return "No detected managers match this view.\n\nb shows the full catalog, including missing managers.\ns opens setup."
		}
		return "No managers match this filter.\n\nEsc clears the filter; s opens setup."
	}
```

```bash
cat >> internal/tui/view.go <<'EOF'

// secondaryColumn formats the right-hand column for the visible rows, padding
// provider and installed-version parts so update arrows line up.
func (m *Model) secondaryColumn(rows []row) []string {
	out := make([]string, len(rows))
	providerWidth, installedWidth := 0, 0
	withProvider := m.view != managersView
	for _, r := range rows {
		if withProvider && r.manager != "" {
			providerWidth = max(providerWidth, ansi.StringWidth(providerLabel(r.manager)))
		}
		if m.view == updatesView {
			installed, _, _ := strings.Cut(clean(r.secondary), " → ")
			installedWidth = max(installedWidth, ansi.StringWidth(installed))
		}
	}
	for i, r := range rows {
		secondary := clean(r.secondary)
		if m.view == updatesView {
			if installed, latest, ok := strings.Cut(secondary, " → "); ok {
				secondary = line(installed, installedWidth) + " → " + latest
			}
		}
		if withProvider && r.manager != "" {
			secondary = line(providerLabel(r.manager), providerWidth) + " · " + secondary
		}
		out[i] = secondary
	}
	return out
}

// columnWidths gives the right column its full content width when it fits and
// otherwise keeps a readable label before truncating the right column.
func columnWidths(rows []row, secondaries []string, available int) (int, int) {
	labelNeed, rightNeed := 1, 1
	for i, r := range rows {
		labelNeed = max(labelNeed, ansi.StringWidth(clean(r.label)))
		rightNeed = max(rightNeed, ansi.StringWidth(secondaries[i]))
	}
	right := rightNeed
	if labelNeed+1+rightNeed > available {
		right = max(1, available-1-min(labelNeed, max(available/3, 16)))
	}
	return max(1, available-1-right), right
}

func updateBadge(kind domain.UpdateKind) string {
	switch kind {
	case domain.UpdateMajor:
		return "MAJOR"
	case domain.UpdateMinor:
		return "minor"
	case domain.UpdatePatch:
		return "patch"
	case domain.UpdateRevision:
		return "rev"
	}
	return ""
}

func updateBadgeStyle(kind domain.UpdateKind) lipgloss.Style {
	switch kind {
	case domain.UpdateMajor:
		return warningStyle.Bold(true)
	case domain.UpdateMinor:
		return accent
	}
	return muted
}
EOF
```

```bash
	content := ansi.Strip(updatesFixture(t, 200).View().Content)

			arrows[ansi.StringWidth(l[:i])] = true
		}
	}

		t.Fatalf("arrows not aligned: %v\n%s", arrows, content)
	}
}
```

```bash
func (m *Model) secondaryColumn(rows []row, budget int) []string {
	out := make([]string, len(rows))
	providerWidth, installedWidth, latestWidth := 0, 0, 0
	withProvider := m.view != managersView
	for _, r := range rows {
		if withProvider && r.manager != "" {
			providerWidth = max(providerWidth, ansi.StringWidth(providerLabel(r.manager)))
		}
		if m.view == updatesView {
			installed, latest, _ := strings.Cut(clean(r.secondary), " → ")

			latestWidth = max(latestWidth, ansi.StringWidth(latest))
		}
	}
	if versions := budget - providerWidth - 6; budget > 0 && installedWidth+latestWidth > versions {
		installedWidth = max(1, min(installedWidth, max(versions/2, versions-latestWidth)))

	for i, r := range rows {

			if installed, latest, ok := strings.Cut(secondary, " → "); ok {
				secondary = line(installed, installedWidth) + " → " + latest
			}
		}
		if withProvider && r.manager != "" {
			secondary = line(providerLabel(r.manager), providerWidth) + " · " + secondary
		}
		out[i] = secondary
	}
	return out
}
```

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-15 14:24:56Z)**_

兩個問題都改好了，還沒 commit。

**Git 進度**：落後 3 個 commit 不是因為 awesome list 收錄，而是你自己在 origin 上的 v0.1.3/v0.1.4 commit（binary 發佈、Homebrew symlink 修正）。我已經用 fast-forward 把 `main` 跟到最新（你本地 `.specstory` 的改動有自動保留），然後開了 `feat/update-kind-columns` 分支，在上面開發。

**1. 分辨大版本更新和小 patch**
- 新增 `internal/domain/updatekind.go`，把每個更新分成 `major` / `minor` / `patch` / `revision`。
  - `4.0.0 → 4.0.0_1`、或 cask 只有逗號後面的 build 變了，算 `revision`（同一版本重新打包）。
  - 0.x 版本照 semver 的慣例：`0.1.x → 0.2.x` 算 major，`0.3.0 → 0.3.3` 算 minor。
  - 日期版本（ca-certificates、certifi、cloudflared 這類）和讀不懂的版本不標，避免一堆誤報的 MAJOR。
- **Updates 畫面**：每列最右邊有標籤，`MAJOR` 是黃色粗體、`minor` 是藍色、`patch`/`rev` 是灰色。標題那行會顯示統計，例如 `Item · 311 · 42 major · …`。
- 用 `/major` 可以只看大版本更新；右側 Details 會多一行 `Update type: …`。
- `lazypkg updates` 的表格多了 `TYPE` 欄。
- 這個分類只用來顯示和篩選，不會影響能不能升級或批次選取。

**2. 寬螢幕版本號被截斷**
- 原因：版本那欄寫死最多 25 字（`view.go:259`），多出來的寬度全給了左邊套件名稱。
- 現在欄寬依「畫面上看得到的那幾列」的內容來算。寬螢幕下像 `1.21.9,4905428782613504 → 1.22.0,…` 這種長版本會完整顯示。
- provider 和目前版本那兩段都有補齊空白，所以 `→` 會上下對齊。
- 螢幕窄的時候，目前版本和最新版本會平分剩下的寬度，兩邊各自截斷，最新版本不會整個被擠掉。
- Installed / Discover 畫面也一起受惠。

<tool-use data-tool-type="generic" data-tool-name="AskUserQuestion"><details>
<summary>Tool use: **AskUserQuestion**</summary>
**How should 0.x versions be labeled?**

Options:
- **Position only + 0.x hint (Recommended)** - Label by which number changed, the same way for every version: 0.6→0.10 is minor and 0.15.6→0.15.9 is patch. A 0.x minor change gets an extra marker (e.g. `minor!`, colored as risky), and the details pane explains that 0.x may break.
- **Keep the semver 0.x shift** - Keep the current behavior: a 0.x minor change shows MAJOR and a 0.x patch change shows minor. Only add an explanation in the details pane.
- **Position only, no hint** - Label purely by the position that changed and ignore 0.x risk entirely.

**Which sort/filter controls do you want in Updates?** _(select multiple)_

Options:
- **o: cycle sort** - Sort by name → update type (MAJOR first) → provider. Selection is kept by row identity.
- **t: cycle type filter** - Switch between all, major, minor, patch and rev; the current filter shows in the heading. It combines with / and with marks.
- **Relaxed parsing** - Also read 3.6a as 3.6 with suffix a, and label a calendar version whose only change is _N as rev.


**Answer:** 我會選 Option 1：Position only + 0.x hint，但稍微修改它的設計。

對於你這種需要支援各式 CLI、GitHub Release、套件版本的 TUI，我認為最合理的設計是：

把「版本號哪個部分變了」與「更新是否可能破壞相容性」分開表示。

這是因為現在不同生態系確實沒有完全統一的 versioning 習慣。

## 1. 現在主流工具怎麼處理 0.x？

| 規範／生態               | `0.2.0 → 0.3.0`      | 實際意義                     |
| ------------------- | -------------------- | ------------------------ |
| Semantic Versioning | MINOR                | 0.x 不保證 API 穩定           |
| npm / node-semver   | 通常視為相容性邊界            | `^0.2.0` 不會接受 `0.3.0`    |
| Rust / Cargo        | 可視為 breaking release | 0.x minor 具有類似 major 的意義 |
| Go Modules          | 不保證相容                | v0.x 屬於 unstable         |
| Python / PEP 440    | 依版本數字比較              | 不直接推斷 API 相容性            |

這裡最重要的一點是：

SemVer 官方規範其實沒有要求將 0.x 的 MINOR 重新命名為 MAJOR。

它只說 0.x 處於初期開發階段，不提供穩定性保證。Cargo 與 npm 的相容性處理是進一步採用的慣例。

[image](https://www.google.com/s2/favicons?domain=https://semver.org\&sz=32)

Semantic Versioning

+4



因此 Option 2 雖然有實務依據，但如果直接把第二位數變動顯示成 `MAJOR`，對跨生態系的版本瀏覽器來說容易產生歧義。

## 2. 我會推薦這樣顯示

Version change

Classification

1.4.2 → 2.0.0



MAJOR

1.4.2 → 1.5.0



MINOR

1.4.2 → 1.4.3



PATCH

0.2.0 → 0.3.0

⚠ 0.x unstable

MINOR

0.2.3 → 0.2.4

0.x

PATCH

2026.09 → 2026.10



CALVER

示意設計：0.x 的警告表示相容性沒有保證，不代表該次更新已確認包含 breaking changes。

這樣做有三個優點：

- 一致性：MAJOR / MINOR / PATCH 永遠描述數字變化的位置。
- 資訊完整：另外提供 compatibility risk。
- 可擴充：未來支援 CalVer、pre-release、其他非標準版本時，不需要改動既有分類。

## 3. 還有一個很重要的細節：不是所有數字版本都是 SemVer

例如：

| 版本形式             | 建議辨識方式                        |
| ---------------- | ----------------------------- |
| `v1.2.3`         | SemVer                        |
| `v0.6`           | Two-component numeric version |
| `2026.10.15`     | 可能是 CalVer                    |
| `1.2.3-beta.1`   | SemVer pre-release            |
| `1.2.3.post1`    | PEP 440 post-release          |
| `nightly-abc123` | Custom / Unknown              |

特別注意，`0.6` 不是嚴格的 SemVer 2.0（標準要求三個數字段），但在 Python PEP 440 裡完全合法。至於 `2026.10.15`，也不能僅憑格式就確定是 CalVer。

[image](https://www.google.com/s2/favicons?domain=https://semver.org\&sz=32)

Semantic Versioning

+2



因此我會讓內部資料模型至少區分三個維度：

```
version_scheme   semver | pep440 | calver | unknown
change_type      major | minor | patch | prerelease | unknown
compatibility    breaking | compatible | uncertain | unknown
```

其中 `compatibility` 應該依版本規範、package ecosystem 或 release notes 判斷，而不是完全由版本號推論。

## 4. 回到你現在的 CLI 選項

我會這樣選：

1\. Position only + 0.x hint

但將 `minor!` 改成 `MINOR` + 獨立的 `0.x` 警告，避免讓使用者誤會 minor 本身一定是 breaking。

未來再增加顯示模式

`Bump type`（版本位置）與 `Compatibility impact`（相容性影響），讓使用者能選擇不同視角，並分別篩選與排序。

另外，截圖提到的 selected row 把 MAJOR 顏色移除，我也不太建議。選取 highlight 與版本語意應該是獨立的視覺層次，至少要維持一致的 badge 樣式。

總結：如果你的工具目標是通用 CLI / release manager，Option 1 比 Option 2 更合理。 Option 2 可以作為特定 ecosystem 的 compatibility-aware 模式，但不適合當成全域預設。, o: cycle sort, t: cycle type filter". Read the answers carefully — they may request clarification, changes, or that you not proceed — and follow what they actually say.

```text
func (m *Model) switchView(index int) tea.Cmd {
	m.status = ""
	m.filtering = false
	m.input.Blur()
	m.view = viewID(index)
	m.pendingG = false
	m.reconcile(m.view, false)
	if m.view == managersView {
		if !m.managersLoaded && !m.managersLoading {
			return m.loadManagers()
		}
		return m.checkManagerHealth(false)
	}
	s := &m.states[m.view]
	if !s.loading && ((!s.attempted && !s.loaded) || s.needsReload) {
		return m.loadView(m.view)
	}
	if m.view == discoverView {
		return m.ensureInventory(false)
	}
	return nil
}

func (m *Model) clearSearch() {
	m.cancelView(discoverView)
	s := &m.states[discoverView]
	s.snapshot = domain.Snapshot{}
	s.query = ""
	s.acceptedQuery = ""
	s.loaded = false
	s.stale = false
	s.err = nil
	m.reconcile(discoverView, true)
}
```

Rewrite classifier as position + unstable flag

```bash
python3 - <<'EOF'
p='internal/domain/updatekind.go'
s=open(p).read()
s=s.replace('''// UpdateKind describes how far an available version is from the installed one.
// It is derived from version text for display only and never gates an upgrade.
type UpdateKind string

const (
	UpdateMajor    UpdateKind = "major"
	UpdateMinor    UpdateKind = "minor"
	UpdatePatch    UpdateKind = "patch"
	UpdateRevision UpdateKind = "revision" // same upstream version, rebuilt (brew _N, cask build)
	UpdateUnknown  UpdateKind = ""
)
''','''// UpdateKind names which part of the version text changed. It describes the
// version position only, not compatibility, and never gates an upgrade.
type UpdateKind string

const (
	UpdateMajor      UpdateKind = "major"
	UpdateMinor      UpdateKind = "minor"
	UpdatePatch      UpdateKind = "patch"
	UpdatePrerelease UpdateKind = "prerelease"
	UpdateRevision   UpdateKind = "revision" // same upstream version, rebuilt (brew _N, cask build)
	UpdateCalendar   UpdateKind = "calver"
	UpdateUnknown    UpdateKind = ""
)

// UpdateClass separates the changed version position from compatibility
// hints. Unstable marks a 0.x installed version: such releases make no
// stability promise, which does not prove this update breaks anything.
type UpdateClass struct {
	Kind     UpdateKind `json:"kind,omitempty"`
	Unstable bool       `json:"unstable,omitempty"`
}
''')
old=s[s.index("// ClassifyUpdate reports"):s.index("func segment(")]
new='''// ClassifyUpdate reports which version position changed from installed to
// latest. Unparseable or non-increasing versions are UpdateUnknown; versions
// that look calendar-based are UpdateCalendar.
func ClassifyUpdate(installed, latest string) UpdateClass {
	a, okA := parseVersion(installed)
	b, okB := parseVersion(latest)
	if !okA || !okB {
		return UpdateClass{}
	}
	if a.calendar || b.calendar {
		if installed == latest {
			return UpdateClass{}
		}
		return UpdateClass{Kind: UpdateCalendar}
	}
	class := UpdateClass{Unstable: a.numbers[0] == 0}
	for i := range max(len(a.numbers), len(b.numbers)) {
		x, y := segment(a.numbers, i), segment(b.numbers, i)
		if x == y {
			continue
		}
		if y < x {
			return UpdateClass{}
		}
		switch i {
		case 0:
			class.Kind = UpdateMajor
		case 1:
			class.Kind = UpdateMinor
		default:
			class.Kind = UpdatePatch
		}
		return class
	}
	switch {
	case a.pre != b.pre:
		class.Kind = UpdatePrerelease
	case a.revision != b.revision:
		class.Kind = UpdateRevision
	default:
		return UpdateClass{}
	}
	return class
}

'''
s=s.replace(old,new)
s=s.replace('''// UpdateKind classifies the package's installed version against its latest.
func (p Package) UpdateKind() UpdateKind { return ClassifyUpdate(p.Version, p.Latest) }''','''// UpdateClass classifies the package's installed version against its latest.
func (p Package) UpdateClass() UpdateClass { return ClassifyUpdate(p.Version, p.Latest) }''')
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF

import "testing"

func TestClassifyUpdate(t *testing.T) {
	for _, tc := range []struct {
		installed, latest string
		want              UpdateKind
		unstable          bool
	}{
		{"4.0.0", "4.0.0_1", UpdateRevision, false},
		{"4.2.3", "4.4.4", UpdateMinor, false},
		{"2.6.9", "4.0.23", UpdateMajor, false},
		{"1.18.2_1", "1.18.3", UpdatePatch, false},
		{"5.3.15", "5.3.20", UpdatePatch, false},
		{"2.4.28,f3f5cec400aa", "2.4.29,0011bbcc", UpdatePatch, false},
		{"1.1.2156,4e9bb23e", "1.1.2156,5aa00000", UpdateRevision, false},
		{"2026-08-13", "2026-09-01", UpdateCalendar, false},
		{"2026.7.22", "2026.8.1", UpdateCalendar, false},
		{"2026.8.19_1", "2026.8.19_2", UpdateCalendar, false},
		{"v4.26.0", "v4.26.1", UpdatePatch, false},
		{"0.6.0", "0.10.0", UpdateMinor, true},
		{"0.15.6", "0.15.9", UpdatePatch, true},
		{"0.9.9", "1.0.0", UpdateMajor, true},
		{"9.11", "9.12", UpdateMinor, false},
		{"306", "308", UpdateMajor, false},
		{"10.0.203", "10.0.400", UpdatePatch, false},
		{"1.0.0-rc1", "1.0.0", UpdatePrerelease, false},
		{"2.0.0", "1.9.0", UpdateUnknown, false},
		{"1.0", "1.0", UpdateUnknown, false},
		{"", "1.0", UpdateUnknown, false},
		{"3.6a", "3.8", UpdateUnknown, false},
	} {
		got := ClassifyUpdate(tc.installed, tc.latest)
		if got.Kind != tc.want || got.Unstable != tc.unstable {
			t.Errorf("ClassifyUpdate(%q, %q) = %+v, want %q unstable=%v", tc.installed, tc.latest, got, tc.want, tc.unstable)
		}
	}
}
```

```bash
	return strings.ToUpper(string(kind))
}

func updateBadgeStyle(kind domain.UpdateKind) lipgloss.Style {
	switch kind {
	case domain.UpdateMajor:
		return warningStyle.Bold(true)
	case domain.UpdateMinor:
		return accent
	}
	return muted
}

func updateKindSummary(rows []row) string {
	counts := map[domain.UpdateKind]int{}
	unstable := 0
	for _, r := range rows {
		counts[r.update.Kind]++
		if r.update.Unstable {
			unstable++
		}
	}
	var out string
	for _, kind := range updateKindOrder {
		if counts[kind] > 0 && kind != domain.UpdateUnknown {
			out += fmt.Sprintf(" · %d %s", counts[kind], kind)
		}
	}
	if unstable > 0 {
		out += fmt.Sprintf(" · %d 0.x", unstable)
	}
	return out
}
```

```bash
cat > internal/tui/updatesort.go <<'EOF'
package tui

import (
	"cmp"
	"slices"
	"strings"

	"github.com/daviddwlee84/lazypkg/internal/domain"
)

var (
	updateSorts     = []string{"name", "type", "provider"}
	updateFilters   = []string{"all", "major", "minor", "patch", "0.x", "other"}
	updateKindOrder = []domain.UpdateKind{domain.UpdateMajor, domain.UpdateMinor, domain.UpdatePatch, domain.UpdatePrerelease, domain.UpdateRevision, domain.UpdateCalendar, domain.UpdateUnknown}
)

func updateFilterMatches(filter string, class domain.UpdateClass) bool {
	switch filter {
	case "major", "minor", "patch":
		return string(class.Kind) == filter
	case "0.x":
		return class.Unstable
	case "other":
		return class.Kind != domain.UpdateMajor && class.Kind != domain.UpdateMinor && class.Kind != domain.UpdatePatch
	}
	return true
}

// sortUpdateRows orders by the chosen key and falls back to the package ID,
// so selection (kept by row key) stays stable across sort changes.
func sortUpdateRows(rows []row, mode string) {
	byName := func(a, b row) int { return cmp.Compare(strings.ToLower(a.label), strings.ToLower(b.label)) }
	switch mode {
	case "type":
		slices.SortStableFunc(rows, func(a, b row) int {
			return cmp.Or(cmp.Compare(slices.Index(updateKindOrder, a.update.Kind), slices.Index(updateKindOrder, b.update.Kind)), byName(a, b))
		})
	case "provider":
		slices.SortStableFunc(rows, func(a, b row) int { return cmp.Or(cmp.Compare(a.manager, b.manager), byName(a, b)) })
	}
}
EOF
```

兩個 commit 都在 `feat/update-kind-columns` 分支上：

**標籤看起來不一致的原因**：第一版有一條 0.x 規則，0.x 版本的 minor 變動會顯示成 MAJOR、patch 變動顯示成 minor。所以 `serie 0.6→0.10` 是 MAJOR，`zlib 3.2.1→3.2.4` 卻是 patch。

**現在的標籤規則**：照你的設計，「哪一位數變了」和「穩不穩定」分開顯示。

| 範例 | 顯示 |
|---|---|
| `2.6.9 → 4.0.23` | `MAJOR` |
| `0.43.1 → 0.45.1` | `0.x MINOR`（0.x 是獨立一欄） |
| `0.15.6 → 0.15.9` | `0.x PATCH` |
| `1.0.0-rc1 → 1.0.0` | `PRE` |
| `4.0.0 → 4.0.0_1`、只有 cask build 變 | `REV` |
| `2026.3 → 2026.4`、`yt-dlp 2026.8.19_1→_2` | `CALVER` |

- 選中的那一列，標籤也保留原本的顏色，只換背景色。
- Details 改顯示 `Version change: minor`；0.x 套件會多一行說明：沒有穩定性保證，但不代表這次更新確定會破壞相容性。
- CLI 的 `TYPE` 欄位會顯示成像 `minor (0.x)` 這樣。

**排序和篩選（只在 Updates 畫面）**
- `o`：輪流切換排序：名稱 → 類型（MAJOR 在最前）→ provider。
- `t`：輪流切換類型篩選：all → major → minor → patch → 0.x → other。
- 目前的排序和篩選會顯示在標題列，footer 也有按鈕可以用滑鼠點。
- 可以和 `/` 文字篩選一起用；選中的列和勾選都會保留。`U filtered` 只處理目前看得到的列。

````text
# Installation and upgrades

Version **v0.1.4** provides macOS and Linux binaries for amd64 and arm64. Go is
needed only for source builds. Other operating systems are not part of this
binary release. Runtime integrations remain separate from installing this CLI.

```sh
brew install daviddwlee84/tap/lazypkg
lazypkg --version
lazypkg self upgrade --check
lazypkg self upgrade --yes
```

The personal tap consumes complete verified GitHub Releases; a new tag can
precede formula publication. Homebrew owns its installed version and completion
files. Check mode inspects the running executable, receipt, formula and owning
Brew without upgrading or querying GitHub. Apply delegates only that formula,
then verifies the effective installed product/version. A current or pinned
formula can be unchanged. Failure may have partial manager effects; no rollback
or switch of installer is promised. Noninteractive/JSON apply requires `--yes`.

For standalone installs, download the matching `lazypkg_VERSION_OS_ARCH.tar.gz`
from [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/lazypkg/releases), verify its
exact entry in `checksums.txt`, and put the executable on PATH. Bash and Zsh
completion files are included under `completions/`; Homebrew installs them,
while manual archive users can place them in their shell's completion directory.

This release intentionally keeps standalone binary updates external: chezmoi's
`installPersonalTools` registry uses verified binaries on Linux and the personal
tap on macOS. `just upgrade-personal` preserves that installed owner, validates
candidates and refreshes completions. The in-program manager adapter does not
replace a standalone/local build. Never overwrite a Homebrew keg manually or
assume an unrelated PATH copy is the installed executable being updated.

Source installation remains available:

```sh
go install github.com/daviddwlee84/lazypkg/cmd/lazypkg@v0.1.4
# Update an existing Go installation through its original destination:
go install github.com/daviddwlee84/lazypkg/cmd/lazypkg@latest
```

`go install` uses `GOBIN` or `GOPATH/bin`; inspect `go env GOBIN GOPATH` if it is
not on PATH. A moved executable does not follow a later Go install automatically.
Source tags recover their module version; release archives inject v0.1.4; local
checkout builds retain a development identity. `@latest` selects a suitable
version tag, not necessarily the newest main-branch commit.

## Release contract

The tag workflow runs the native test suites and packaging checks before
publishing a complete draft. Each immutable release contains four binary
archives, one rootless source archive and `checksums.txt`. Archives contain only
the binary, MIT license and generated Bash/Zsh completions. Source archives
retain build inputs, tests, embedded assets and documentation, while excluding
development evidence. Go module ZIPs independently exclude evidence through
nested `go.mod` boundaries; neither mechanism rewrites existing Git history.

```sh
goreleaser check
goreleaser release --snapshot --clean --skip=publish,announce
python3 scripts/release.py check --project lazypkg --binary lazypkg --smoke
python3 scripts/check-distribution.py
```

The publisher rejects incomplete sets, checksum/architecture/member mismatches,
and attempts to replace a published asset. Publish a new version for corrections.
The Homebrew tap is the single formula writer. Release automation does not need
a cross-repository token. Native Linux/macOS CI and macOS local verification are
reported separately; cross-builds alone do not prove terminal/backend behavior.
````

**Why `brew upgrade` still said 0.1.4:**
- The tap doesn't update when a release is published. Its "Sync stable formulas" workflow updates it, and that workflow is set to run every hour at :17.
- GitHub has been delaying that schedule: before this, the last run was at 01:23Z, while v0.2.1 was published around 04:21Z. When you ran `brew upgrade`, the tap still had 0.1.4.

**What I did:** I triggered the same sync manually for `lazypkg` only, without changing its settings. The run passed in 1m17s and committed `c3a3ed5 Sync validated stable release formulas` to the tap. The formula's darwin_arm64 download now points to the v0.2.1 file.

The tap's own CI didn't run for that commit, and none of the earlier sync commits triggered it either.

Run this again to upgrade:

`lazypkg self upgrade --check` also works now.

If you don't want to wait for the delayed schedule after future releases, you can trigger the sync yourself right after the release finishes:
